trust_decision.summary: Every authorization decision taken on the request path must use one canonical form of that path: fully percent-decoded (repeatedly, so double encoding collapses), matrix parameters stripped after decoding, NULs removed, backslashes folded to '/', dot segments resolved - so that the path the security layer authorizes is the same path the downstream handler resolves. Decided in HttpSecurityUtils.normalizePath and applied at each path->policy matching site.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary says authentication/authorization bypass via path normalization; the first grep is for the path helper, and the one place that turns a request path into a permission decision in the default RBAC is findHttpMatchers, which calls HttpSecurityUtils.pathWithoutMatrixParams(context.normalizedPath()).

fix_sites.entry_point: shared helper: new HttpSecurityUtils.normalizePath (decode loop, matrix strip, NUL strip, backslash fold, removeDots)
quarkus.http.auth.permission.<name>.paths / @AuthorizationPolicy paths applied to HTTP and JAX-RS (also reused by the management interface): declared paths are normalized when the matcher is built
HTTP path-based RBAC on the main and management listeners (PathMatchingHttpSecurityPolicy, ManagementPathMatchingHttpSecurityPolicy, JaxRsPathMatchingHttpSecurityPolicy all delegate here)
Servlet web.xml <security-constraint> enforcement for the Undertow (servlet) stack
Keycloak policy-enforcer path matching (policyEnforcer.getPathMatcher().matches(...)) on any HTTP request
HttpRequest.getRelativePath() handed to the Keycloak adapter/claims machinery
OIDC static tenant selected by a path segment (DefaultStaticTenantResolver)
OIDC static tenant selected by quarkus.oidc.tenant-paths (PathMatchingTenantResolver)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The reference docs state that a configured HTTP security policy path must not contain ';' and that matrix-parameter-dependent decisions need a custom HttpSecurityPolicy (docs/src/main/asciidoc/security-authorize-web-endpoints-reference.adoc:37-38), so a solver can argue that encoded-semicolon/matrix variants and the non-core consumers (servlet web.xml constraints, the Keycloak adapter's own PathMatcher, OIDC tenant paths, CSRF token path) are an unsupported combination and out of scope.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Literal matrix parameters must still match their segment policy: GET /api/baz;v=1.1, /api/baz;, /api/foo;x=1/bar;y=2 stay bound to the /api/baz and /api/foo/bar authenticated policies, and a permission declared with an encoded path (quarkus.http.auth.permission.baz-percent-enc.paths=/api/baz%3Bv=1.1, fluent httpSecurity.path("/api/baz%3Bv=1.1")) is a legitimate config value. A fix that only decodes (full URIDecoder decode without the post-decode matrix strip) reopens /api/baz;v=1.1, and a fix that normalizes one side only collapses a declared encoded path onto a different path (a permit on /x%3By would then permit /x).

O6_input_shapes: literal matrix parameters on any segment (/a;x=1/b;y=2, trailing ';')
percent-encoded unreserved characters (%69, %6E, %61) and encoded dot segments (%2e%2e)
double and triple encoding (%2569, %252F, %25252F) via a decode loop
literal NUL and encoded %00 null bytes
backslash used as a path separator (literal '\\' and %5C)
configured policy paths that themselves contain encoded characters (normalized on the config side)

O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: That helper is the documented 'normalized and decoded path' and is already used by the static-resource handlers (StaticResourcesRecorder.java:65,100); a maintainer writing another path-based policy would reach for it and get decode-only, no matrix stripping - the exact half-fix that keeps /api/baz;v=1.1 open.
